title: Photographing the Microscopic: Winners of Nikon Small World 2026
text:
Daniel Knop, Oberzent-Airlenbach, Hessen, Germany

 Image of Distinction: A close view of the leg of a weevil

 Eric Epstein, Brooklyn, New York, U.S.

 Sixth Place: Hemitrichia slime-mold spore structures (fruiting bodies)

 Dr. Marcel Clemens, Verona, Veneto, Italy

 Eighth Place: Pencil lead during exposure to a high-voltage electrical discharge

 Amartya Tashi Mitra and Paul Maier, Aria Huang, Nathaniel Sweet and Anthony Wokasch, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio, U.S.

 Honorable Mention: Neurons of red-eared-slider ( Trachemys scripta ) embryo

 Nicolas Noel and Dr. Valentina Cigliola, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, Tennessee, U.S.

 Image of Distinction: Neonatal-mouse astrocyte in culture

 Anne Gleich, Licoi, Kaiserslautern, Rheinlandpfalz, Germany

 Image of Distinction: Daphnia sp. (water flea) and Volvox sp. (green algae)

 Přemysl Orlík, Opava, Czech Republic

 Image of Distinction: Hazelnut weevil ( Curculio nucum )

 Gerhard Vlcek, Maria Enzersdorf, Austria

 Image of Distinction: Cross-section of spruce treetop

 Zhang You, Kunming, Yunnan, China

 Image of Distinction: A weevil pokes its head out of a hole it bored into a fava bean.

 Amartya Tashi Mitra and Harsha Sen, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio, U.S.

 Image of Distinction: Cellular structures of slipper-limpet ( Crepidula fornicata ) larva

 Kaelin Wulf and Ms. Rachel Flannery, Allen Institute, Seattle, Washington, U.S.

 Third Place: Neurons in an expanded mouse brain

 Dr. Arlene Wechezak, Anacortes, Washington, U.S.

 Image of Distinction: Red algae, diatoms, and protozoans

 Justin Zoll, Freeville, New York, U.S.

 Image of Distinction: Adult fungus gnat caught in the sticky trichomes of a cannabis plant

 Be sure to visit the Nikon Small World competition website to view the full set of winning and honored images.
